submission.justification: PROVISIONAL recommendation: Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage. It gives the highest simulated light at every coverage from 5% to 30%. At 30% it gives 50.95 PE/MeV, against 36.96 for D2 and 24.4 for D3. That is a lead of about 38% over D2, which is well above the apparent scatter in the simulation. Light did not saturate. The fitted exponent is about 0.78, and the feedthroughs allow up to 30%. This does NOT show that the hard reliability requirement is met. No project document reports thermal-cycling failure fractions (20 cycles, 300 K to 87 K), sample sizes or test conditions for any design. All three designs are unverified, and none is shown to fail either. D1's thin bonded dichroic filter is a speculative thermal-cycling risk, but that is not data. D2 is also unverified, so it is not a verified fallback. The simulation models light only, gave no error bars, and each point is a single run. Before the Q3 design freeze, run 20-cycle thermal tests with an adequate sample size on D1 and D2, and ideally D3. Modules cannot be replaced once the cryostat is filled. Also repeat the simulations with different seeds to quantify the noise. If D1 fails the test, switch to D2 at 30% if it passes, and otherwise to D3.

[s4 summary] I recorded the conclusions with `record_results`. No design is documented to pass the reliability requirement, so I can't pick a winner among passing designs. I read the light-collection numbers from the earlier steps and ran no new simulations.

- **Reliability:** None of the three designs has thermal-cycling data (≤5% failures after 20 cycles, 300 K to 87 K). All three are unverified, and none is documented as failing.
- **Best light:** D1 gives the most light at every coverage. D1 at 30% reaches 50.95 PE/MeV, ahead of D2 at 36.96 and D3 at 24.41.
- **Saturation:** Gains slow down but don't saturate. The fitted exponents are about 0.77 to 0.79, close to the 0.8 in the 2025 summary. D1 still gains about 6 PE/MeV from 25% to 30%. Feedthroughs allow 30%, so 30% is usable.
- **Robustness:** D1 leads D2 by about 34–40%, which is 10–14 PE/MeV. That is well above the apparent scatter. D2's 25% point sits about 3 PE/MeV below the smooth trend. The simulation gave no error bars and only one run per point, so the noise is not actually measured.
- **Recommendation and fallback:** D1 at 30% is a provisional choice, conditional on thermal-cycle test data. D1's bonded filter is a speculative reliability risk, and D1 is the top-ranked design. The fallback is D2 at 30%, but D2 is also unverified, so it is not a verified fallback.

Two things are needed before the Q3 design freeze:
- Thermal-cycle tests with an adequate sample size for D1 and D2.
- Repeat simulations with different seeds to quantify the noise.

[s5 summary] I recorded the final recommendation, but it comes with a major caveat. No design has thermal-cycling evidence, so none is shown to meet the 5% failure limit.

- **Recommendation:** Module-D1 at 30% wall coverage, with a simulated 50.95 PE/MeV. This is provisional. It is the best-light choice, and it depends on thermal-cycle test data.
- **Runner-up:** Module-D2 at 30%, with 36.96 PE/MeV. D1 leads D2 by about 38%. D3 is third at 24.4 PE/MeV.
- **Reliability evidence:** There is none. No project document gives failure fractions, sample sizes or test conditions for 20 cycles from 300 K to 87 K. All three designs are unverified, and none is shown to fail either.
- **Risk to D1:** Its thin bonded dichroic filter is a possible thermal-cycling risk, but that is speculation, not data. D2 is also unverified, so it is not a verified fallback.
- **Simulation limits:** The simulation models light only. It gave no error bars, and each point is a single run. D2's 25% point sits about 3 PE/MeV below the smooth trend, so the noise is probably a few PE/MeV.
- **Before the Q3 design freeze:** Modules can't be replaced once the cryostat is filled, so thermal-cycle tests with an adequate sample size are needed for D1 and D2, ideally D3 as well. Repeating the simulations with different seeds would also quantify the noise.

If D1 fails the test, switch to D2 at 30% if it passes, and otherwise to D3.
